thread:
sofia: Heads-up 10min sync. I'm sketching an RFC follow-up to split the bench runner into 'probe' (fast, local) and 'golden' (full infra). Goal: let integrators validate perf without pulling heavy corpora.

omar: Love that. How do the two modes differ contract-wise?

sofia: Probe mode will require a minimal "probe_handshake": `capabilities`, `seed`, `warmup_hint`. Golden mode keeps the current heavy contract. Probe returns a fixed small sample and a warmup blob.

jia: Two concerns: 1) probe determinism across kernels, 2) ensuring probe results map to golden. We should record kernel metadata and quantization flags in the probe telemetry.

trent: Agreed on kernel metadata. Also suggest a monotonic scoring mapping: if probe latency improves by X%, predict expected golden delta with a linear model per family before we accept any rollout.

sofia: Good idea. We'll collect historical probe->golden deltas to fit family-specific slopes. For rollout gating, require predicted golden 99p latency change < 4% and observed golden delta within 2x predicted during canary.

omar: For adapters: do we version the handshake or keep a capability flag? I'd prefer capability flags so older runtimes still work.

sofia: Capability flags + an adapter version header. Runtime will fallback depending on support. We'll add `probe_supported: true` and `adapter_version: "v1.1"` to the capabilities.

jia: For local dev UX: `rbin probe --short --seed=7` should emulate a canary probe. If adapter doesn't support probe, runner should fall back to a cached probe artifact and warn.

trent: Add a telemetry counter for fallback usage; if >1% of production probes fallback, fail the rollout.

sofia: Rollout plan: land probe adapter, enable shim (translates probe->golden) behind a flag, canary on a small dedicated slice for 12h, run probe and golden in shadow for models in the slice, compare mappings.

omar: Shadow testing is key. Also capture failure modes: missing warmup blob, empty probe sample, or inconsistent seed behavior. Define failure categories and automatic rollback thresholds.

sofia: I'll enumerate these. Proposed auto-rollback triggers: 1) probe failure rate > 0.5% in canary, 2) golden-prediction error > threshold for 5 minutes, 3) kernel mismatch causing >3% 99p latency regressions.

jia: Minor item: ensure precise timestamps included in probe payload for reproducibility. Also include `probe_variant` label (e.g., short, medium) so tests are comparable.

trent: Ops tasks: need a short runbook snippet to toggle flags and extract quick metrics. I can draft the commands.

sofia: Please paste them here when ready. Also opening ticket MLON-4321 for the split and MLON-4322 for telemetry schema.

trent: Snippet:
```bash
# enable probe canary
curl -X POST $CTRL/api/flags -d '{"name":"probe_canary","state":"on","target":"dedicated-slice-7"}'
# sample probe metrics
rquery metrics 'service=probe_runner AND model=mosaic-7b' --agg=percentile(99,latency)
# check fallbacks
rquery metrics 'event=probe_fallback' --agg=count --window=15m
# rollback
curl -X POST $CTRL/api/flags -d '{"name":"probe_canary","state":"off"}'
```
sofia: Perfect. I'll add the runbook steps and failover playbook. One last ask: telemetry schema needs fields: `probe_seed`, `probe_variant`, `kernel`, `quant_flag`, `adapter_version`, `fallback` (bool). Jia can you own the schema PR?

jia: On it. I'll include dimension cardinality guidance to avoid high-cardinality explosion for the `probe_variant` labels.

omar: Can we also capture a short raw sample hash to detect data drift without sharing PII?

sofia: Yes: `sample_hash` (sha256) is fine. We'll store only the hash.

onboard-bot: Note: created ticket MLON-4321 (bench split) assigned to sofia; MLON-4322 (probe telemetry) assigned to jia. Scheduled reminder: canary-check @sofia in 24h.

sofia: Thanks folks, I'll post the RFC follow-up doc link once I push the PR. Quick thumbs if we're aligned.

jia: :thumbsup:

omar: :thumbsup:

trent: :thumbsup:
